Borrowed from Latin iuvenīlis, derived from iuvenis (“young”). By surface analysis, joven (“young”) + -il (“-ile”).

chain.g: A youth, a young man, young woman, young adult (between ages 20-40), (older than an adulescens but younger than a senior/senex)

ety.text: Inherited from Latin iuvenis, from Proto-Italic *juwō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂yéwHō (“young”). Compare Galician xove, Spanish joven.

senses.d: Most recently begun or formed.
ex: I may be the youngest in my family but I still resent being referred to as the baby.

senses.d: Receiving dealt cards last, i.e. immediately before the next deal to the eldest.
The youngest child in a family, or individual in a group.

ety.text: From the biblical character Benjamin.
From the biblical Benjamin, the youngest son of Jacob.
